quiz.question_en: What is the main role of `%w` in `fmt.Errorf`?
options_id: Menambahkan konteks sambil tetap mempertahankan error asal dalam chain
options_en: It converts an error into a warning
It adds context while preserving the original error in the chain
It prints the error without a return value
It compares two errors

quiz.question_id: Mengapa wrapping berguna ketika error muncul jauh di dalam call stack?
quiz.question_en: Why is wrapping useful when an error occurs deep in the call stack?
options_id: Karena wrapping menghapus error asli agar caller tidak bingung
Karena wrapping menambahkan konteks tentang operasi yang gagal tanpa kehilangan error awal
Karena wrapping mencegah fungsi return error nil
Karena wrapping membuat semua error menjadi sentinel
options_en: Because wrapping removes the original error so callers are not confused
Because wrapping adds context about the failed operation without losing the original error
Because wrapping prevents functions from returning nil errors
Because wrapping turns all errors into sentinels

quiz.question_id: Apa hasil cetak umum dari `fmt.Errorf("loadApp: %w", err)` ketika `err` adalah `file not found`?
quiz.question_en: What is the usual printed result of `fmt.Errorf("loadApp: %w", err)` when `err` is `file not found`?
options_en: `file not found: loadApp`
`loadApp: file not found`
`%w loadApp file not found`
Only `loadApp`

quiz.question_id: Apa yang dikembalikan `errors.Unwrap(wrapped)` untuk error yang dibungkus satu level?
quiz.question_en: What does `errors.Unwrap(wrapped)` return for an error wrapped one level deep?
options_id: Error yang langsung dibungkus di dalamnya
options_en: The outer context string
The directly wrapped inner error
The entire error chain at once
Always `nil` for errors created by `fmt.Errorf`

quiz.question_id: Jika error dibungkus beberapa kali, apa yang dipertahankan oleh wrapping chain?
quiz.question_en: If an error is wrapped several times, what is preserved by the wrapping chain?
options_id: Jalur konteks bertingkat beserta akses ke error yang dibungkus
Tidak ada; tiap wrapping mengganti total error sebelumnya
options_en: Only the outermost error
Only the innermost error message
A layered context path together with access to the wrapped errors
Nothing; each wrap completely replaces the previous error

quiz.question_en: When is `%v` more appropriate than `%w` in `fmt.Errorf`?
options_id: Saat caller tidak perlu atau tidak boleh menginspeksi error asal melalui chain
options_en: When the caller does not need or should not be able to inspect the original error through the chain
When you want to support `errors.Unwrap`
When all errors are sentinels
When the error is nil

quiz.question_id: Apa trade-off dari selalu memakai `%w` untuk semua error?
quiz.question_en: What is the trade-off of always using `%w` for every error?
options_id: Tidak ada trade-off; `%w` selalu paling tepat
Anda mungkin tanpa sengaja mengekspos detail atau identitas error internal yang tidak ingin dijadikan kontrak API
options_en: There is no trade-off; `%w` is always the right choice
You may accidentally expose internal error details or identities that you do not want to become part of your API contract
The program will no longer compile
The error can no longer be printed

quiz.question_id: Apa manfaat menulis konteks seperti `getProfile: %w` daripada hanya mengembalikan `err`?
quiz.question_en: What is the benefit of writing context like `getProfile: %w` instead of just returning `err`?
options_id: Menjelaskan lapisan operasi mana yang gagal ketika error sampai ke level atas
Mengubah error menjadi custom type otomatis
options_en: It makes the error nil
It explains which operation layer failed when the error reaches higher levels
It automatically turns the error into a custom type
It removes the need for `if err != nil`

quiz.question_id: Jika `original := errors.New("disk full")` lalu `wrapped := fmt.Errorf("write failed: %w", original)`, mana yang benar?
quiz.question_en: If `original := errors.New("disk full")` and then `wrapped := fmt.Errorf("write failed: %w", original)`, which is true?
options_en: `errors.Unwrap(wrapped) == original` is true
`wrapped == original` is always true
`wrapped.Error()` contains only `disk full`
`wrapped` is no longer of type error

quiz.question_id: Pernyataan mana yang paling tepat tentang error wrapping di Go?
quiz.question_en: Which statement is most accurate about error wrapping in Go?
options_id: Wrapping menggantikan kebutuhan error handling lokal
Wrapping terutama untuk menambah konteks sambil menjaga kemampuan inspeksi terhadap error asal bila diperlukan
Wrapping membuat semua error menjadi comparable dengan `==`
options_en: Wrapping replaces the need for local error handling
Wrapping is primarily for adding context while preserving the ability to inspect the original error when needed
Wrapping is only relevant to panics
Wrapping makes all errors comparable with `==`
